**This is the most useful issue you can open here.** The maintainer's own daily
use is the fastest signal this project has, and until the retirement rule was
written it could only come out positive. Evidence that cannot come out negative
is not evidence.

## Which procedure

`ledger` / `fit` / `cascade` / `timing` — or the router in `SKILL.md` if the
problem is that the wrong one was chosen.

## What you asked

The turn that triggered it, as close to verbatim as you can share.

## What it did

What the procedure produced, and what you would have wanted instead.

## Which of these it was

- [ ] It fired when it should not have (an ordinary turn got a decision procedure)
- [ ] It did not fire when it should have
- [ ] It fired and routed to the wrong procedure
- [ ] It routed correctly and the answer was still worse than thinking directly
- [ ] It handed back labelled blocks instead of a recommendation

- Tool (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) and version:
